Submitted. Summary of what happened:

**Search process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront: stop if best-so-far Sharpe > 1.2, stop after ≥4 failures, or restart if last gain ≤ 0.02.
- Called `init`, which anchored on the single best feature (feature 1, long) and immediately achieved in-sample Sharpe **1.3139** — already above my 1.2 stop bar.
- Attempted `extend_best` to add a second feature and stress-test robustness, but it was refused because my `best_so_far_above` rule had already fired.
- Honored the pre-declared rule rather than switching trigger mid-stream just to keep digging (which would have marked the rest of the run as not replayable), and called `stop`.

**Lesson/caveat:** Because the rule fired on the very first move, I never got to exercise `extend_best`'s output, `swap_worst`, `refine`, or the required `pick` comparison — the bar I set (1.2) turned out to be too close to what a single raw feature already delivered. That's a genuine miscalibration on my part in setting the trigger, and it left the final specification thinner (single feature) than I'd have liked.

**Final specification:** long position in feature **1** alone, in-sample annualized Sharpe net of costs = **1.3139**.

**OOS prediction:** mean Sharpe **0.60**, sd **0.50** — a substantial haircut from the in-sample figure, reflecting that single-feature in-sample Sharpes of this magnitude typically don't fully survive out-of-sample, and wide uncertainty since the search was truncated before any robustness checks (pick/swap/refine) could be performed.
